source.publication: 2025 Schedule M1M Income Additions and Subtractions
source.section: Form M1 lines 1-4, 7-10 (instructions PDF p.13 Standard Deduction Table for Line 4, p.14 Worksheet A, p.39 Tax Rate Schedules, pp.32-38 tax table); Schedule M1M line 12 and Worksheet for line 12 steps 1-30 (M1M PDF p.3, p.4)

worked: Separate return, spouses lived together: 2,000 wide steps from 54,160, benefits 85% taxable from the first dollar. The alternative is reduced but loses. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages 40,000.00 + taxable Social Security 17,000.00 = 57,000.00. Social Security benefits (Form 1040 line 6a) 20,000.00; line 6b taxable 17,000.00 (federal worksheet: benefits taxable up to 85%; given, not tested). Federal taxable income = 57,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction (15,750 plus 0 x 1,600) = 41,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form M1, married filing separately: line 1 federal AGI 57,000.00. Schedule M1M line 1 other-state municipal interest 0.00; line 10 additions 0.00; Form M1 line 2 0.00; line 3 = 57,000.00. Schedule M1M line 12, Worksheet: step 1 57,000.00; step 2 54,160.00; step 3 2,840.00; step 4 2,840.00 / 2,000 rounded up = 2; step 5 0.2; step 6 17,000.00; step 7 3,400.00; step 8 = 13,600.00 (step 29, Tier 1 step 26 is 0.00). Keep share 0.8. Alternative method, projection: measure = federal AGI + tax-exempt interest = 57,000.00 + 0.00 = 57,000.00; cap first: lesser of 17,000.00 and 2,920.00 = 2,920.00; less 20% x (excess over 44,315.00, 12,685.00) = 2,537.00; alternative = 383.00. Worksheet steps 9-24 as printed: steps 9-11 57,000.00 - 17,000.00 = 40,000.00; steps 12-13 50% x 20,000.00 = 10,000.00; step 14 0.00; step 15 50,000.00; steps 16-18 0.00; step 19 50,000.00; step 20 44,315.00; step 21 5,685.00; step 22 1,137.00; step 23 2,920.00; step 24 1,783.00; step 25-27 17,000.00; step 28 1,783.00; step 30 greater of 1,783.00 and 13,600.00 = 13,600.00. Line 12 = the better of the two, 13,600.00. The projection's alternative entry loses, so only the simplified amount is applied. Schedule M1M line 16: no one is 65 or older (born before January 2, 1961), so no Schedule M1R subtraction. Schedule M1M line 40 = Form M1 line 7 subtractions = 13,600.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 = 13,600.00 (lines 12, 16, 17, 25). State income before deduction = 57,000.00 - 13,600.00 = 43,400.00. Standard Deduction Table for Line 4 (PDF p.13): base 14,950.00; AGI is not over 119,475.00, so no Worksheet A. Line 4 = 14,950.00. Form M1 line 8 total = 14,950.00 + 13,600.00 = 28,550.00; line 9 Minnesota taxable income = 57,000.00 - 28,550.00 = 28,450.00. Line 10 tax from the rate schedule (PDF p.39): 5.35% x (23,810.00 - 0.00) = 1,273.835 + 6.80% x (28,450.00 - 23,810.00) = 315.52 = 1,589.355. The tax table (PDF pp.32-38) gives 1,589; expected keeps the schedule formula. Line 16 credits 0.00; state income tax 1,589.36.
accepted_approximations: The alternative Social Security method tests federal AGI plus tax-exempt interest, the nearest available measure. Worksheet step 19 uses total income less taxable benefits plus 50% of all benefits, which no projection measure holds. The cap is applied before the reduction; the worksheet takes the lesser of the reduced cap and taxable benefits.
Tax comes from the rate schedules at every income; below 86,800 of taxable income the booklet requires its 100-wide tax table.
